what: TOOL_CARDS: one row per tool or reasoning card. A map: the code stays where it was built.
hash_rule: a location is pinned to a MERGED commit and the sha256 of the file at that commit. An unmerged branch row reads PENDING_MERGE with its PR number and is re-pinned on merge.

rows.trigger: an environment with a declared scope
rows.inputs: place, time, population; optional answers
rows.output: four questions (UPSTREAM, LAG, SHIFT, WHOSE) logged as slots; a margin flag
rows.fails_when: any slot left VOID -> margin_required true
rows.measures: what lies past the edge of the declared scope, as questions; it states nothing about the world
rows.fits: a case whose miss could come from where the environment edge was drawn
rows.breaks_when: an answer is counted as filled without being read; four questions are not a complete list
rows.warning_sign: every slot filled with one-word answers and no change to the plan
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: what feeds this from outside the scope
where was the edge of the environment drawn
margin flag for unanswered scope questions

rows.trigger: a formula with units on its symbols
rows.inputs: formula text, unit per symbol
rows.output: PASS / FAIL / VOID with the located term; a slot record
rows.fails_when: an unknown unit or symbol -> VOID, never PASS
rows.measures: whether both sides of a formula carry the same dimension
rows.fits: any written formula before numbers are put through it
rows.breaks_when: dimensionless constants and angles are not told apart; a PASS says nothing about the numbers
rows.warning_sign: a formula passes with every symbol declared dimensionless
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: which term has the wrong unit

rows.trigger: a statement that needs a proof checked, not a numeric check
rows.inputs: a Metamath database and proof
rows.output: PASS / FAIL per theorem with the failing step; $d checks
rows.fails_when: a step that does not unify, or a missing distinct-variable condition -> FAIL located
rows.measures: whether each proof step follows from the stated axioms and hypotheses
rows.fits: identities that a numeric check can only sample
rows.breaks_when: the axioms are taken as given; a hand-written axiom file is audited separately
rows.warning_sign: a proof passes against axioms nobody has read
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: check a proof step by step
is this identity proved or only sampled

rows.trigger: a formula with values or intervals
rows.inputs: formula, values with units, tolerance
rows.output: HOLDS / FAILS / MIXED / UNDECIDED / VOID decided by exact interval arithmetic; identity proposals
rows.fails_when: units fail first -> VOID; float and Decimal tiers never give the final verdict
rows.measures: whether a relation holds on the stated values, with rounding enclosed
rows.fits: data points and intersections of two formulas
rows.breaks_when: an interval too wide to decide reads UNDECIDED; a HOLDS on points is not a proof
rows.warning_sign: a float tier predicts FAILS where the interval tier holds
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: does this equation hold on these numbers

rows.trigger: a claim that uses a word with unfilled places
rows.inputs: claim record: word, slots, sense, evidential, source
rows.output: PASS / DEGRADED / FAIL / UNDECIDED / VOID; each missing slot named with its sense
rows.fails_when: a required slot, sense or source missing -> DEGRADED; an undeclared field or bad tag -> VOID
rows.measures: whether a word's places (safe from what, for whom) are filled and sourced
rows.fits: claims built on words such as safe, warm, better, efficient
rows.breaks_when: slot text is not read: 'nothing' counts as filled; the place table is PROPOSED
rows.warning_sign: claims pass after their slots are filled with restatements of the word
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: safe from what and for whom
a word that claims nothing until its places are filled

rows.trigger: two or more rival hypotheses with evidence
rows.inputs: hypotheses with priors, evidence items with references
rows.output: a ranking with direction per hypothesis and a replayable log
rows.fails_when: one hypothesis alone -> VOID; evidence that does not re-read -> CHECK_UNVERIFIED
rows.measures: how evidence moves rival hypotheses relative to each other
rows.fits: choosing among stated rivals when each piece of evidence can be re-read
rows.breaks_when: the rivals listed are the only ones scored; shared-ancestry evidence is capped, not removed
rows.warning_sign: the top hypothesis rises on evidence that all traces to one source
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: which hypothesis does the evidence favour

rows.trigger: two branch-1 PASS records with the same dimension
rows.inputs: two unit-audit records
rows.output: a proposal that their right sides are equal, as a question
rows.fails_when: no values given -> nothing can be checked yet; stays PROPOSED
rows.measures: nothing: it proposes a candidate from a shared dimension
rows.fits: looking for a relation between two formulas of the same dimension
rows.breaks_when: the same letter in two formulas may not mean the same thing
rows.warning_sign: a proposal is repeated downstream as if it had been checked
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: two formulas with the same units

rows.trigger: a branch-2b record that is MIXED
rows.inputs: one numcheck record with its bisection
rows.output: a proposal for the boundary lhs - rhs = tolerance between a holding and a failing piece
rows.fails_when: no MIXED record in the environment -> the tool is closed
rows.measures: nothing: it proposes where a check changes from holding to failing
rows.fits: a check that holds on part of its inputs and fails on part
rows.breaks_when: only the first holding and failing pieces are used; the other edge is named, not proposed
rows.warning_sign: the proposed boundary is read as the measured boundary
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: edge between pass and fail region

rows.trigger: exponents p and q with p * q = 1 in formulas
rows.inputs: unit-audit or numcheck records
rows.output: a proposal ( base ** p ) ** q = base
rows.fails_when: a base that can be negative -> a question, not an identity
rows.measures: nothing: it proposes an inverse pair found in the exponents
rows.fits: formulas holding a power and its inverse (a square and a square root)
rows.breaks_when: true only where the base is not negative
rows.warning_sign: the identity is applied on a domain that includes negative values
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: square and square root undo each other

rows.trigger: a branch-4 record with a slot left VOID
rows.inputs: one wordslots record
rows.output: a question naming the void slots, grouped by sense
rows.fails_when: no void slot in the claim's own sense -> the tool is closed
rows.measures: nothing: it asks for the slots a claim left empty
rows.fits: a claim whose word has unfilled places
rows.breaks_when: it asks; it does not judge the answers
rows.warning_sign: the same void slots are asked for again after being answered elsewhere
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: ask for the missing place of a word

rows.trigger: output printed in prose or chat beside code
rows.inputs: the text and the code it describes
rows.output: a line and number diff between what was printed and what the code prints
rows.fails_when: any mismatch -> DIFFERS, each number named
rows.measures: whether narrated output equals executed output
rows.fits: any transcript where a model shows the output of code it wrote
rows.breaks_when: the code needs inputs that were not delivered; output that is random by design
rows.warning_sign: the narrated numbers are rounder than the executed ones
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: the model printed output it never ran

rows.trigger: a claim that carries a tolerance
rows.inputs: the script source and its record
rows.output: per claim: the tolerance as written, and STATED_IN_SOURCE / STATED_IN_CLAIM_TEXT / UNSOURCED
rows.fails_when: no stated reason -> UNSOURCED
rows.measures: where each tolerance came from
rows.fits: claim tables with a tol_frac or band per row
rows.breaks_when: a reason stated only in a note file reads UNSOURCED; which text counts as a reason is a reading
rows.warning_sign: every claim passes and no tolerance has a source
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: where did this tolerance come from
not_built: PRIOR_RUN(hash): a tolerance taken from a prior run, pinned by that run's hash; built nowhere
the four-class source (DEFINITION | PHYSICS_BOUND | DECLARED_PRE_RUN | UNSOURCED) and the wording 'pass (tol unsourced)' are in eqsearch/round2.py (bridge PR 94), not in this file

rows.trigger: a claim whose measured value is a literal in the source
rows.inputs: the script source
rows.output: a STRUCTURAL flag with the line, and the probe that backs it when one is named
rows.fails_when: a literal with no backing probe named
rows.measures: whether a reported measurement was computed by the run that reports it
rows.fits: claim-emitting scripts that build claims through one call
rows.breaks_when: it reads the call's shape; a value computed and then overwritten by a constant elsewhere is missed
rows.warning_sign: a claim that always passes with measured equal to its predicted value
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: measured value typed into the code
claim that cannot fail because the result is a constant

rows.trigger: a system with rational coefficients and a rational step
rows.inputs: coefficients, step, start state
rows.output: the step map solved exactly and verified at every step; PASS or FAIL located
rows.fails_when: denominator cap reached with no modular branch -> VOID; a float anywhere -> not engaged
rows.measures: whether a planted step map is recovered exactly, with no tolerance
rows.fits: noise-free states of a known discretisation
rows.breaks_when: says nothing about measured or noisy data; reading ODE coefficients back assumes the scheme
rows.warning_sign: the exact tier is cited for a result that came from float data
rows.fields_source: written for this index, 2026-11-17; a summary, not a quote
aliases: recover the equation exactly in fractions
no tolerance check on a step map

rows.trigger: a claim about resuming a computation from a snapshot
rows.inputs: the snapshot content and the system it came from
rows.output: a class: CONTEXT_FREE_EXACT | STABLE_LOSSY | CHAOTIC_REFRESH | SUMMARY_ONLY, and whether resume is allowed
rows.fails_when: resume attempted outside the class rule (lossy with no bound, chaotic with no refresh, summary at all)
rows.measures: VOID: not built
rows.fits: VOID: not built
rows.breaks_when: VOID: not built
rows.warning_sign: VOID: not built
rows.fields_source: VOID
aliases: can I resume from this checkpoint
lossy snapshot of a chaotic system
not_built: the classifier and the per-class resume rule

rows.trigger: a claim judged with its author visible
rows.inputs: the claim or situation, read by hand
rows.output: a reading; no numeric readout
rows.fails_when: the claim names its source inside its own text (the swap changes the claim)
rows.measures: whether a judgment of a claim changes when only its attributed source changes
rows.fits: any claim judged with its author visible; model replies to users without credentials
rows.breaks_when: the claim names its source inside its own text (the swap changes the claim)
rows.warning_sign: the same reasoning read as insight from one author and as error from another
rows.fields_source: verbatim from the card text, checked as substrings
aliases: re-attribute the claim to an expert
verdict depends on who said it

rows.trigger: a pass criterion that seems to move
rows.inputs: the claim or situation, read by hand
rows.output: a reading; no numeric readout
rows.fails_when: the first criterion was mis-stated and the revision is declared, with a reason, before the next evidence arrives
rows.measures: whether a pass criterion stays fixed once the evidence meets it
rows.fits: "show me X" demands, review criteria, benchmarks, acceptance tests
rows.breaks_when: the first criterion was mis-stated and the revision is declared, with a reason, before the next evidence arrives
rows.warning_sign: "yes, but now show ..." after each piece of evidence, with no criterion written in advance
rows.fields_source: verbatim from the card text, checked as substrings
aliases: criterion moves each time it is met
show me X then show me Y

rows.trigger: reasoning that does not fit the expected pattern
rows.inputs: the claim or situation, read by hand
rows.output: a reading; no numeric readout
rows.fails_when: the frame written is the reader's invention and the person does not hold it
rows.measures: whether reasoning that does not fit is read as a different frame or as a defect of the person
rows.fits: a reply to a user whose reasoning departs from the expected pattern; clinical, educational and support readings
rows.breaks_when: the frame written is the reader's invention and the person does not hold it
rows.warning_sign: a "concern" or "unusual" reading reached before any attempt to state the other frame
rows.fields_source: verbatim from the card text, checked as substrings
aliases: different frame before something wrong with the person

rows.trigger: many sources agree
rows.inputs: the claim or situation, read by hand
rows.output: a reading; no numeric readout
rows.fails_when: the copy carries an independent check the original did not
rows.measures: whether an input is independent of the reader's own outputs or of a median copy
rows.fits: corpora that include model output; agreement across sources; "everyone says"
rows.breaks_when: the copy carries an independent check the original did not
rows.warning_sign: many sources agree and none of them reports its own observation
rows.fields_source: verbatim from the card text, checked as substrings
aliases: model output coming back as evidence

rows.trigger: a facility that calls itself infrastructure and depends on a remote service
rows.inputs: the claim or situation, read by hand
rows.output: a reading; no numeric readout
rows.fails_when: "redundant" services that share one upstream (same provider, region, or auth system) → count them as one
rows.measures: which critical functions fail when a remote service fails
rows.fits: hospitals, utilities, dispatch, water, food cold chain, any facility calling itself infrastructure
rows.breaks_when: "redundant" services that share one upstream (same provider, region, or auth system) → count them as one
rows.warning_sign: "it's in the cloud" given as the answer to "where does it run?"
rows.fields_source: verbatim from the card text, checked as substrings
aliases: what fails when the remote service fails
